# Repeated compound-border row spacing

Original OPC/XML fixture generated by `tools/compound_row_rounding_fixture.py`.
It reuses the repository's original minimal package skeleton, with no corpus
content, artwork, external engine or added fonts. Installed Arial is required
for native/browser text measurements.

Fifteen pages isolate nine repeated rows per case, with zero vertical cell
margins, exact 12pt paragraph lines and centered text. Cases cover nil/single/
thinThickLargeGap borders at minimum and exact row heights, plus ten large-gap
border sizes (0, 2, 8, 11, 12, 13, 17, 24, 48, 96 eighth-points). Only every
third row has top/bottom borders. This separates accumulated border allocation
from font leading, content-driven row growth and exact-row behavior.

The reference application exported `native.pdf` after read-only opening and
explicit repagination using `tools/export-reference.ps1`. All 135 PDF row
baselines are recorded in `reference.json` by `tools/record_compound_row_pdf.py`;
the manifest binds both source and PDF hashes. `native-positions.json` is an
additional in-memory Range.Information capture made by
`tools/record_compound_row_rounding.ps1`. Those API positions have coarser
screen-unit rounding and are not used as precise baseline assertions.

The reference application reserves 45 + floor(size * 2.5) twips for each large-gap compound border:
1.5pt and .75pt fixed bands plus a declared gap truncated to whole twips.
Painted bands remain 1.44pt and .72pt, with the previously established 600-DPI
gap quantization and nonzero minimum. Size zero therefore reserves 2.25pt
while painting 2.28pt; size 24 reserves 5.25pt while painting 5.16pt. Odd
sizes distinguish fractional-twip truncation from unrounded eighth-points.

Using paint width for row allocation produced up to 1.03pt baseline error in
the original 150-line comparison. Separating allocation and painting reduces
that maximum to 0.131pt. Browser checks cover every row baseline within .2pt,
page count, no-edit package preservation, text editing, unrelated-part
preservation, exact undo and export/reopen. Existing mixed-border, frame,
corner and opposing-border references remain regression controls.

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.4.38, 17.4.66, 17.4.80 and 17.18.2 describe the border
and row declarations. The two-stage numerical allocation/rasterization rule
is measured reference behavior, not an explicit formula in those clauses.
